correctness.rationale: Re-read the actual primary source six-compartment SDE (2.2) and Section 6.1 Milstein formula. The published model has b_I=φE−(μ+γ+φ1)I whereas the printed Milstein drift is b_I−βSI/N; their difference is exactly −βSI/N, nonzero when β,S,I>0,N>0. Independently reconstructed all six drift terms and simplified their sums: stated model gives Λ−μN−φ1 I, printed update gives the same minus βSI/N, proving a spurious total-population sink. Setting all stochastic coefficients to zero exhibits a deterministic Euler O(Δt) inconsistency, not a stochastic Milstein correction; a rational witness β=1/20,S=I=1,N=2 gives −1/40. The source later prints a correct ANN Euler infected drift without the extra incidence sink. The claim concerns print, not unknown program code.

value.rationale: This exposes a structural, first-order discretization defect in a published six-compartment stochastic epidemic model, not merely a cosmetic typographical issue. An artificial susceptible-to-exposed incidence loss in the infected equation violates the model population-balance identity, so the printed numerical scheme approximates a different drift even with arbitrarily small steps. The exact term and minimal correction matter for mathematical and numerical reproducibility of this named model.

limitations: Only the printed Milstein formula is assessed; authors may have used different code.
The comparison does not prove any full stochastic trajectory or extinction/persistence figure incorrect.
